1.title: What it means to attribute a P&L

4.title: Correlated indicators and the value of a subset

nodes.label: Shapley 1953
nodes.title: A value for n-person games
nodes.summary: A few axioms on how a value treats players fix a unique split of a cooperative game's worth. Each player receives its marginal contribution averaged over random orders of arrival.

nodes.label: Aumann 1974
nodes.title: Values of Non-Atomic Games
nodes.summary: On a specified class of non-atomic games, the value is uniquely determined and can be represented by integrating marginal contributions along the diagonal of the coalition space.

nodes.label: Owen 1977
nodes.title: Values of Games with a Priori Unions
nodes.summary: Owen's value allocates a cooperative game's total through an exogenously specified partition, averaging the orders of unions and the orders of players within each union.

nodes.label: Brinson 1985
nodes.title: Measuring non-U.S. equity portfolio performance
nodes.summary: The active return of an international equity portfolio over its benchmark splits exactly, market by market, into a country-allocation term, a within-country stock-selection term and a cross product, and the three sum to the portfolio return minus the benchmark return.

nodes.label: Brinson 1986
nodes.title: Determinants of Portfolio Performance
nodes.summary: On 91 US pension plans over 1974-1983, a passive policy portfolio built from long-run asset weights and index returns explains on average 93.6% of the time-series variance of each plan's quarterly return, while active timing and selection lost 1.10% a year on average.

nodes.label: Perold 1988
nodes.title: The implementation shortfall: Paper versus reality
nodes.summary: The gap between a costless "paper" portfolio, traded at the midprice prevailing when each decision is taken, and the real portfolio is an exact, additive sum of an execution cost on the trades done and an opportunity cost on the trades not done, and only this before-trade measure captures both.

nodes.label: Sharpe 1992
nodes.title: Asset allocation: Management style and performance measurement
nodes.summary: A fund's *style* can be estimated from its returns alone by regressing them on a small set of investable asset-class indices with weights constrained to be nonnegative and sum to one; the residual, measured out of sample against that style mix, is the manager's selection return.

nodes.label: Litterman 1996
nodes.title: Hot Spots and Hedges
nodes.summary: Portfolio risk splits exactly into each position times its marginal risk. This split, not each position's own volatility, shows where risk comes from and which trades hedge it best.

nodes.label: Grinold 2000
nodes.title: Active Portfolio Management: A Quantitative Approach for Producing Superior Returns and Controlling Risk
nodes.summary: The book builds active management on a structural factor model of risk and uses it to decompose ex ante risk into additive contributions, to attribute ex post active return to factors and a specific residual, and to evaluate a signal through the portfolio it produces.

nodes.label: Lipovetsky 2001
nodes.title: Analysis of regression in game theory approach
nodes.summary: Taking the R^{2} of OLS regressions on every subset of predictors as the characteristic function of a cooperative game, the Shapley value splits the full-model R^{2} into nonnegative shares that stay stable under bootstrap when predictors are strongly correlated, where OLS coefficients and their "net effects" are unstable and can be negative.

nodes.label: Castro 2009
nodes.title: Polynomial calculation of the Shapley value based on sampling
nodes.summary: Averaging marginal contributions over uniformly sampled player orders gives unbiased Shapley estimates, and the proposed precision calculation uses a normal approximation.

nodes.label: Grinold 2011
nodes.title: Breadth, Skill, and Time
nodes.summary: Breadth in the fundamental law is the rate at which a signal's information turns over times the number of assets. A signal's IC therefore depends on the horizon over which it is measured.

nodes.label: Guéant 2013
nodes.title: Dealing with the inventory risk: a solution to the market making problem
nodes.summary: With a bound on inventory, the classical market-making problem reduces to a finite system of linear differential equations. Its solution gives the optimal quotes, which over long horizons depend only on inventory.

nodes.label: Maleki 2013
nodes.title: Bounding the Estimation Error of Sampling-based Shapley Value Approximation
nodes.summary: Concentration bounds based on the range of the marginal contributions make the precision of permutation sampling explicit, and stratifying by coalition size allocates samples according to these bounds.

nodes.label: Menkveld 2013
nodes.title: High frequency trading and the new market makers
nodes.summary: An accounting identity splits one high-frequency trader's P&L into net spread earned and a loss on its positions. The trader earns the spread and gives part of it back on inventory held longer than a few seconds.

nodes.label: Durin 2014
nodes.title: Signal-wise performance attribution for constrained portfolio optimisation
nodes.summary: When a convex optimiser is driven by a sum of signals, active constraints and L1 costs become extra quadratic terms at the optimum. Positions, P&L, risk and costs then split exactly into one portfolio per signal.

nodes.label: Owen 2014
nodes.title: Sobol' Indices and Shapley Value
nodes.summary: For independent inputs, an input's Shapley share of variance lies between the variance it explains alone and the variance it adds last (two Sobol' indices).

nodes.label: Barber 2015
nodes.title: Controlling the false discovery rate via knockoffs
nodes.summary: A synthetic "knockoff" copy of each variable, with the same correlations, gives a selection threshold that controls the false discovery rate in finite samples. The basic construction needs a Gaussian linear regression with at least twice as many observations as variables.

nodes.label: Cartea 2015
nodes.title: Algorithmic and High-Frequency Trading
nodes.summary: The book treats market making as stochastic control and splits the market maker's value into cash, inventory at the midprice and the value of quoting. Inventory risk and adverse selection shift the optimal quotes and the target inventory.

nodes.label: Lundberg 2017
nodes.title: A Unified Approach to Interpreting Model Predictions
nodes.summary: Six local explanation methods share one additive form; within it, only Shapley values of the model's conditional expectation have local accuracy, missingness and consistency. The paper calls them SHAP and gives estimators such as Kernel SHAP.

nodes.label: Lehalle 2018
nodes.title: Market Microstructure in Practice
nodes.summary: For a practitioner, execution performance is measured against a benchmark chosen to fit the investment style and broken down into the terms of an Almgren–Chriss-type mean-variance cost; market impact grows concavely with participation rate and duration, and the market maker appears only through stylised models, not through an explicit P&L decomposition.

nodes.label: Lehalle 2019
nodes.title: Incorporating signals into optimal trading
nodes.summary: Adding a Markovian price-drift signal to a linear transient-impact execution model keeps the problem strictly convex; for an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck signal, the optimal schedule is a liquidation part, linear in the initial inventory, plus a signal part, linear in the initial signal.

nodes.label: Covert 2020
nodes.title: Understanding Global Feature Contributions With Additive Importance Measures
nodes.summary: SAGE values a feature set by how much it reduces a fixed model's expected loss and takes the Shapley value of that game. It equals the average of SHAP values of the loss and unifies several global importance measures.

nodes.label: Gu 2020
nodes.title: Empirical asset pricing via machine learning
nodes.summary: On 60 years of US stocks, regularised nonlinear predictors (trees, and above all shallow neural networks) beat linear benchmarks in out-of-sample return prediction, the gain is traced to predictor interactions, and all models rank the same small group of signals (price trends, liquidity, volatility) as most important.

nodes.label: Virtu Financial 2020
nodes.title: Multi-Asset Transaction Cost Analysis
nodes.summary: A two-page vendor brochure that lists the features of Virtu's commercial TCA service across equities, FX, fixed income and futures; it describes no method.

nodes.label: Covert 2021
nodes.title: Improving KernelSHAP: Practical Shapley Value Estimation Using Linear Regression
nodes.summary: Pairing each sampled coalition with its complement and estimating the uncertainty make KernelSHAP more practical; a population-design version of the estimator is unbiased.

nodes.label: Jethani 2022
nodes.title: FastSHAP: Real-Time Shapley Value Estimation
nodes.summary: FastSHAP trains a network to predict Shapley values directly, so that each later explanation takes one forward pass.

nodes.label: Mitchell 2022
nodes.title: Sampling Permutations for Shapley Value Estimation
nodes.summary: Structured permutations can reduce the integration error of Shapley estimates; estimator bias, generation overhead and the cost of evaluating the game are separate questions.

nodes.label: Musco 2025
nodes.title: Provably Accurate Shapley Value Estimation via Leverage Score Sampling
nodes.summary: Leverage-score sampling approximates the Shapley regression objective with high probability, with an error bound set by the game's regression residual.

nodes.label: Méloux 2025
nodes.title: The Dead Salmons of AI Interpretability
nodes.summary: Interpretability methods give plausible explanations even for randomly initialised networks, because the questions they answer are not identifiable. The authors treat each method as a statistical estimator and test it against random networks as null models.

nodes.label: Paleologo 2025
nodes.title: The Elements of Quantitative Investing
nodes.summary: The book treats ex post performance attribution as an estimation problem: the factor/idiosyncratic split of P&L carries a computable standard error, and the P&L credited to each of several correlated factors changes with their rotation while the total does not.
